messages:
alex.dev: Hey team — after upgrading our Node client from 0.23.1 -> 0.24.0 a bunch of calls that used to work are returning 404s. Specifically chat.create and session.create. Minimal repro below.

alex.dev: Repro steps:
1) npm i @redwood/inference@0.24.0
2) const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
3) await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: 'hello' })

alex.dev: Error: 404 Not Found - route 'chat.create' not found. Headers show: x-rw-sdk-version: 0.24.0, x-rw-request-id: r-91b2.

alex.dev: Workaround: pinning back to 0.23.1 immediately fixes it. We rolled this into prod and hit a retry loop and billing spike. Need root cause and rollback plan. :grimacing:

zoe.support: Thanks for the report, Alex. Can you paste the exact request payload and the request id from the failing response? I'll escalate to runtime if it looks like a routing mismatch.

alex.dev: Request id r-91b2 attached above. Payload is exactly: `{ model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: 'hello' }` (no session or meta). The 0.23 client used to add `route: 'chat.create'` in the request body under the hood; 0.24 seems to be sending `route: 'chatCreate'` (camelCase) per our logs.

mike.runtime: @zoe.support, pinged. If SDK changed the route name enum it can cause API path mismatch — we do strict route verification in the control plane. I see a spike in 404s around 3602468000-3602468200 in the feed; likely this is the same.

julia.devex: Alex can you share package-lock or yarn.lock snippet showing resolved @redwood/inference version? Need to confirm no transitive mix of packages. Also which region (us-west/us-east/eu)?

alex.dev: Lockfile: `@redwood/inference@0.24.0` resolved. Region: us-west-2. We only saw it in one service at first but then our autoscaler retried on error and caused a lot of requests.

zoe.support: Thanks. Mike — do we have an API change log that would explain removing/renaming 'chat.create'?

mike.runtime: Checking git tags and control-plane diffs. There was no intentional route rename. However, SDK 0.24.0 changed the client-side route mapping generator (codegen) — it now strips dots and uses camelCase for local method names but should still send canonical route keys. If it's sending camelCase as the route identifier that's a bug in the SDK mapping layer.

mike.runtime: Quick mitigation: we can add a tolerant fallback on the server side to accept known camelCase variants for a short window, but that requires a canary deploy and careful rollout.

zoe.support: Can you confirm whether the failing requests include an `X-Client-Route` header or only send the route in body? If header exists we might patch edge to map it.

alex.dev: No header, route is in body under `route` field. Example failing request body: `{ route: 'chatCreate', args: { model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: 'hello' } }`. Old working body: `{ route: 'chat.create', args: { ... } }`.

mike.runtime: That explains it. Edge/router does strict lookup. I can push a quick edge shim that maps `chatCreate` -> `chat.create`, `sessionCreate` -> `session.create` and similar for common ones. That should restore traffic quickly. Will need ~20m to validate and roll to us-west-2.

alex.dev: Appreciate it. Are there any billing implications from those retries we should prepare to dispute? We got charged for dozens of failed attempts due to our client's retry policy.

zoe.support: Documenting this ticket for billing review. Please keep the request ids (r-91b2 and others) — we'll pass to billing for credits. Also, can you temporarily disable client retries (set retry to 0) as part of mitigation?

alex.dev: Done — set retry policy to zero and redeployed, reducing traffic. Will keep pinned to 0.23.1 until fix is live.

mike.runtime: Edge shim rollout started to canary in us-west-2. I'll post when done and include a diff of the mapping rule.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started: edge-shim-route-mapping - run id e-7745 - region us-west-2

mike.runtime: Canary looks good for 5m — no errors for previously failing request ids. Pushing to 50% then 100% in us-west-2.

deploy-bot: rollout update: 50% -> in-progress

mike.runtime: Rollout complete at 100% in us-west-2. Patch maps the top 30 route variants and logs unmapped variants to a special stream for follow-up.

zoe.support: Alex, can you test again with 0.24.0 unpinned and confirm?

alex.dev: Testing now... `await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: 'hi' })` -> 200 OK. Request id r-91c8. Looks fixed from our side.

alex.dev: One more ask: please include a note in the SDK release docs about the codegen mapping quirk and recommend a compatibility guideline. It bit us because our CI auto-upgraded minor versions.

julia.devex: Will do. We'll add a compatibility note + a semver advisory. Also adding a changelog entry explaining route key invariants and recommending pinning patch versions until codegen is validated.

zoe.support: Billing team: request ids for credit review: r-91b2, r-91b3, r-91b5, r-91b9. Billing: please track.

mike.runtime: Follow-up: opening a runtime issue to add tolerant parsing for route keys at router layer and adding unit tests to catch codegen regressions. Also adding an alert if >0.5% 404s for route lookup in a minute.

alex.dev: Thanks all. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :raised_hands:
